Final verification bar: 0 redundant / 13 legitimate / 0 unclassifiable dual-hook entries on the deployed index.

memory_candidates.content: jq footgun: `$arr | index(.)` (or any `X | index(.)` / `X | any(. == .)` pattern piped into a builtin) rebinds `.` to the piped-in value INSIDE the argument expression, so it does not test membership of the outer context's `.` -- it silently tests the array against itself. Always bind the value to a named variable first (`. as $c | ...`) and compare with `any(. == $c)` or `index($c)` instead of relying on bare `.` inside a piped builtin's argument.

Under `set -euo pipefail`, a helper function whose body is a pipeline (e.g. `jq ... | sort -u`) that may legitimately fail (missing file, bad input) will abort the ENTIRE calling script if invoked inside a `var="$(fn)"` command substitution -- pipefail propagates the failing command's exit status through the pipeline, and set -e treats that as the whole statement failing. A later `return 0` inside the function does not help; the abort happens before it runs. Fix by appending `|| true` directly to the pipeline itself (not merely wrapping the function call), so the degrade-gracefully path is reachable.

Never run a bare, unscoped `git stash` / `git stash pop` in a repo where other sessions may be concurrently editing files -- it scoops up every uncommitted tracked change repo-wide, not just the caller's own work, and a concurrent edit landing between stash and pop can cause the pop to abort with conflicts (git's safe default: it leaves both the stash and the working tree untouched). If a stash is taken by mistake, recover only the caller's own affected files via `git show stash@{N}:<path>` and a direct file write/copy, leaving the stash entry itself untouched (never `git stash drop`/`pop`) so concurrent sessions' in-flight work is never at risk.

When representing an optional/degraded lookup result as a jq object built from bash variables, prefer OMITTING the key when the value is absent (`{} + (if $v == "" then {} else {key: $v} end)`) rather than setting the key to an empty array/string. An empty array is a valid, present value that can vacuously satisfy set-difference or subset tests (`[] - $x == []` is always true), silently misclassifying "missing/degraded" as "present but empty" wherever the consumer checks `.key // null == null` to detect absence.
